\section{Gaussian Space --- Invariance --- Replacement}

\subsection*{Gaussian Space --- Invariance --- Replacement: Introduction}
Independent affine inputs can be integrated separately from a common background, yielding fourth-order scalar and single-coordinate replacement estimates.

\subsection*{Gaussian Space --- Invariance --- Replacement: Results}

\begin{theorem}[Integral Formula for an Independent Affine Input]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.independent_affine_integral}
\leanok
\difficulty{5}
Let $(\Omega,\mu)$ be a probability space, and let $A,D,W\colon\Omega\to\mathbb R$ be
measurable up to null sets, with $W$ independent of the pair $(A,D)$. If
$\psi\colon\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ is continuous and $\psi(A+DW)$ is integrable, then the
function $q(a,d)=\mathbb E[\psi(a+dW)]$ is integrable under the distribution of $(A,D)$,
and $\mathbb E[\psi(A+DW)]=\int_{\mathbb R^2}q(a,d)\,d\mathcal L(A,D)(a,d)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Fourth-Order Affine Replacement Bound]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.independent_affine_replacement_bound}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.HasInvarianceMoments, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.affine_replacement_bound, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.independent_affine_comparison_bound, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.integrable_mul_pow_of_memLp}
\difficulty{5}
Let $(\Omega,\mu)$ be a probability space, and let $A,D,U,V\colon\Omega\to\mathbb R$.
Suppose $A,D\in L^4(\mu)$, and suppose each of $U,V$ has mean zero, second moment one,
third moment zero, and fourth moment at most $9$ (in particular, each is measurable up
to null sets with finite fourth absolute moment). Assume each of $U,V$ is independent of
$(A,D)$. Let $\psi\in C^4(\mathbb R)$, and suppose $C\ge0$ bounds $|\psi^{(4)}(t)|$ for
every $t\in\mathbb R$. If $\psi(A+DU)$ and $\psi(A+DV)$ are integrable, then
$\left|\mathbb E\psi(A+DU)-\mathbb E\psi(A+DV)\right|\le (3C/4)\mathbb E[D^4]$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Error from replacing one polynomial input]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.single_coordinate_replacement_bound}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.HasInvarianceMoments, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.Invariance.coordinateDerivative, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.Invariance.coordinateFree, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.Invariance.coordinate_parts_eq_of_off_coordinate, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.Invariance.eval_coordinate_split, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.Invariance.indep_coordinate_parts, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.independent_affine_replacement_bound, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integrable_test_of_memLp_four, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.invariance_coordinate_fourth_moment, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.evalMultilinearRV, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.evalMultilinearRV_memLp, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.MultilinearPolynomial, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.MultilinearPolynomial.HasDegreeAtMost, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.MultilinearPolynomial.eval, BooleanAnalysis.influence}
\difficulty{5}
Let $n,k$ be nonnegative integers, let $(\Omega,\mu)$ be a probability space, and let
$F$ be a real coefficient family on subsets of $\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$ whose coefficients
vanish on sets of size greater than $k+1$. Fix a coordinate $i$, and let
$X_j,Y_j:\Omega\to\mathbb R$ be two coordinate families, each independent within itself,
such that $X_j=Y_j$ as functions whenever $j\ne i$. For every coordinate, both inputs
satisfy the fourth-order invariance moment conditions: their first and third moments are
zero, their second moment is one, and their fourth moment is at most $9$ (with finite
fourth moment and almost-everywhere measurability). If $\psi\in C^4(\mathbb R)$,
$C\ge0$, and $|\psi^{(4)}(t)|\le C$ for every real $t$, then $\left|\mathbb
E[\psi(F(X))]-\mathbb E[\psi(F(Y))]\right|\le \frac{C}{12}9^{k+1}\,\mathrm{Inf}_i[F]^2$,
where $F(X)(\omega)=\sum_S F(S)\prod_{j\in S}X_j(\omega)$ and the influence is that of
the Boolean-cube evaluation of $F$.
\end{theorem}

\subsection*{Gaussian Space --- Invariance --- Replacement: Further results}

\begin{theorem}[Independent Affine Comparison Bound]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.independent_affine_comparison_bound}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.independent_affine_comparison_bound}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.independent_affine_integral}
\difficulty{4}
Let $(\Omega,\mu)$ be a probability space, and let $A,D,U,V\colon\Omega\to\mathbb R$ be
measurable up to null sets, with the pair $(A,D)$ also measurable up to null sets.
Suppose $U$ and $V$ are each independent of $(A,D)$. Let $\psi\colon\mathbb R\to\mathbb
R$ be continuous, and suppose $\psi(A+DU)$ and $\psi(A+DV)$ are integrable. Let
$B\colon\mathbb R^2\to\mathbb R$ be measurable with $B(A,D)$ integrable, and suppose for
every $(a,d)\in\mathbb R^2$ that $\left|\mathbb E[\psi(a+dU)]-\mathbb
E[\psi(a+dV)]\right|\le B(a,d)$. Then $\left|\mathbb E[\psi(A+DU)]-\mathbb
E[\psi(A+DV)]\right|\le\mathbb E[B(A,D)]$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Third-Order Affine Replacement Bound]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.independent_affine_replacement_bound_c3}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.independent_affine_replacement_bound_c3}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.affine_replacement_bound_c3, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.independent_affine_comparison_bound}
\difficulty{4}
Let $(\Omega,\mu)$ be a probability space, and let $A,D,U,V\colon\Omega\to\mathbb R$,
with $(A,D)$ measurable up to null sets and $D,U,V\in L^3(\mu)$. Suppose $U$ and $V$
have equal means and equal second moments, and each is independent of $(A,D)$. Let
$\psi\in C^3(\mathbb R)$, and suppose $|\psi^{(3)}(t)|\le C$ for every $t\in\mathbb R$.
If $\psi(A+DU)$ and $\psi(A+DV)$ are integrable, then
\[\left|\mathbb E\psi(A+DU)-\mathbb E\psi(A+DV)\right|\le \frac C6\left(\mathbb E|U|^3+\mathbb E|V|^3\right)\mathbb E|D|^3.\]
\end{theorem}
